institutionName: UiT The Arctic University of Norway

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Something different from Denmark. Both in the case of the weather and the culture. I also wanted to go to a place that had beautiful nature.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really liked the nature close to where I lived and the experiences away from school. But the university was not the best for me. I only had one course I really liked. But that course was one of the best I've ever had. I also got some new friends and found some new hobbies.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was not the easiest, but I managed. The day of arrival changed a few times, which made it difficult to book the tickets. But everything about where to get the key, and where to meet the first day was okay.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The orientation week was fun but the days were too long. I was put in a group with people from our own country, which makes it hard to socialize with others in the first week.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very easy for me. I got a place a month before.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You can not live on campus. All the student houses around the island are good. They are all the same. But some places don't have kitchen utensils - which was problematic and stressful in the first week.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Nobody told us that it should be printed out. Luckily for me, I already had printed it out.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was just part of the orientation week, which was super nice!

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Some students came with recommendations for nice hikes and were to buy second-hand stuff.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got kicked out of one course because there were too many, and they preferred Norwegian students from UiT over exchange students. But I got an excellent new class so that was okay but very stressful at the beginning of my stay abroad.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read the course description very closely! Apply for all the courses you want, so you can change them before the deadline if needed.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I thought there would be more marine courses that didn't just were about fish.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I also took a course on master-level, which was the best!

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Almost the same. Just fewer seminars and more lectures.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
BIO-2506 Introduction to fish biology
BIO-2508 Aquaculture I
BIO-3009 Arctic Marine Pollution

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
BIO-3009 Arctic Marine Pollution 
That was very interesting! Sophie which is the leader of the course is so nice! The topics are very important, and you learn a lot about what is happening in the arctic right now. I can really recommend it!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I lost my key and had to pay for a new one.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything was more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is a lot to do in Tromsø!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Almost everything. I didn't need anything else.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Climbing, hiking, group sessions at "Kraft" (Sportscenter close to uni) (especially the power yoga). The facilities are excellent and the people are sweet and friendly!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: In summer: hikes. Just explore the nature around the island. Rent a car, and sleep in a DNT cabin. Go whale watching at Skjervøy in the winter ("explore70degrees" is a good company).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was okay. There are a lot of exchange students, so a bit difficult to involve with locals.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Samskipnaden (the Student Welfare Organisation) had a lot of trips and activities for free.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: It is just like home, so not the biggest difference.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Read your course description very carefully before applying to it 
- Get a membership at kraft and the climbing center
- Explore as much as you can

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just be openminded and try not to stress about school, enjoy our stay.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The experiences in the nature

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The school - I think it depends on which courses you take, but I found it challenging.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
